## 4. Clocks, resets and clock-domain crossings

- Clocks: `byte_clk`, `pix_clk`, `tx_byte_clk`.
- Resets: `byte_rst_n`, `pix_rst_n`, `tx_byte_rst_n`.
- Clock and reset behaviour, and any clock-domain crossing, as described in section 6.
- Every clock domain: name, frequency, source, the logic on it. Every reset: one per domain, synchronous active low inside the domain, entering the domain only through a reset synchroniser (asynchronous assertion, synchronous release); reset sequencing between domains has a single, documented source.
- Every clock, reset and signal boundary uses a clock-domain crossing technique, listed in the file header. Never sample another domain's signal directly; never pass a multi-bit value through independent single-bit synchronisers. Example techniques:

| Technique | Use for | Library module |
|-----------|---------|----------------|
| Two- (or more) flop synchroniser (`async_reg`) | single slow level signal (enable, status, IRQ level) | `bit_sync` |
| Pulse synchroniser (toggle, sync, edge detect) | one-clock event / pulse | `pulse_sync`, `toggle_sync` |
| Reset synchroniser (async assert, sync release) | a reset entering a clock domain | `reset_sync`, `reset_ctrl` |
| Asynchronous FIFO with Gray-coded pointers | data stream at any rate ratio | `async_fifo`, `axis_async_bridge` |
| Request / acknowledge handshake (2- or 4-phase) | occasional multi-bit word, register access | `axi4_lite_cdc`, `clock_domain_bridge` |
| Multi-cycle path formulation (hold data, sync a qualifier) | multi-bit value that changes rarely | `cdc_sync_bit` + held register |
| Gray-code counter | counter value read in another domain | inside `async_fifo` |
| Glitch-free clock gate / mux | stopping or switching a clock | device BUFGCE / BUFGMUX, `clk_gen` enables |
| Related clocks from one PLL (fixed phase) | serializers, e.g. 10:1 TMDS, 7:1 LVDS | `clk_gen` outputs of one oscillator |

- Constrain every crossing (false path / max delay on the synchroniser's first flop) and document it.

## 5. Interfaces

- **s_axil_*** - AXI4-Lite slave, address [14:0], 32-bit data: interface `axil_if.slave` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axil_if.sv`).
- **ins_m_axis_t*** - AXI4-Stream master (output), tdata [23:0], tlast, tuser (when `VP_INSERT`): interface `axis_if.master` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv`).
- **ins_s_axis_t*** - AXI4-Stream slave (input), tdata [23:0], tlast, tuser (when `VP_INSERT`): interface `axis_if.slave` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv`).

Bus ports follow the library's SystemVerilog interfaces, one definition file per type: AXI4-Stream `axis_if` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv`, modports master / slave / monitor) and AXI4-Lite `axil_if` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axil_if.sv`, modports master / slave). Icarus Verilog cannot drive members of interface arrays and Yosys reads interfaces only through sv2v, so keep discrete ports (<prefix>_tdata, <prefix>_awaddr, ...) and put the interface and modport in a comment line directly above each port group: `// s_axis: axis_if.slave (ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv), DATA_W = 24`. ## 6. Function

Implement exactly this behaviour (from the reference design's specification):

```text
MIPI CSI-2 camera to HDMI / DVI video pipeline. Version 1.0.0.

byte_clk | pix_clk
D-PHY -> csi2_rx -> axis_async_bridge -> csi2_raw_unpack -> isp_blc_wb
  -> isp_dpc -> isp_demosaic -> isp_ccm -> isp_gamma -> isp_csc
  -> [scaler_bilinear | bypass] -> axis_to_video -> hdmi_tx  -> TMDS (HDMI / DVI)
                                                 -> lvds_tx  -> OpenLDI (LVDS panel)
                                                 -> dsi_tx   -> MIPI DSI (panel)
                                                 -> csi2_tx  -> MIPI CSI-2 (processor)
vid_timing_gen drives axis_to_video (genlock to the camera) and hdmi_tx;
isp_stats taps the linear RGB after the CCM for AE / AWB software.
eof_in_o / eof_out_o pulse at the end of every frame leaving
csi2_raw_unpack (first stage) / entering axis_to_video (last stage),
e.g. for a frame counter.

Every function can be bypassed (BYPASS register, applied at the next
frame start): black level, white balance, defect correction, demosaic
(raw value on R, G and B), CCM, gamma (linear 10 -> 8 bit), CSC (RGB
out), scaler (stream routed around it). CTRL.TPG replaces the whole
pipeline output with colour bars.

The D-PHY analog front end is vendor IP: connect its per-lane HS byte
outputs (PPI) to lane_data_i / lane_valid_i. The TMDS symbols leave on
tmds*_o for a 10:1 serializer (tmds_serializer or vendor OSERDES) and
differential output buffers.

No frame buffer: the display is genlocked to the camera (CTRL.LOCK), so
the display line time must be at least the camera line time; insert an
external frame buffer (axis_dma + DRAM) before axis_to_video for
independent frame rates.

AXI4-Lite (pix_clk), ADDR_W = 15 (src/video_pipeline_map_pkg.sv):
0x0000-0x01FF pipeline registers, 0x4000-0x7FFF the scaler's own map
(scaler_ctrl, base 0x4000).
  0x000 ID          RO "VPIP"; 0x004 VERSION RO ASCII "d.dd"; 0x008 DATE RO BCD
                    mm/dd/yyyy (the ID block); register k of the old map is at
                    0x10 + 4 k (src/include/video_pipeline_regs.sv / .json / .md):
  0x014 CTRL        [0] output enable [1] HDMI (0 = DVI) [2] TPG
                    [3] genlock [5:4] CFA (0 RGGB 1 GRBG 2 GBRG 3 BGGR)
                    [6] CSC BT.709 (0 = BT.601)
                    [7] insert: route the stream after isp_csc out
                    through ins_m_axis_* and back in on ins_s_axis_*
                    (`VP_INSERT; taken at the next frame start)
  0x018 BYPASS      [0] BLC [1] WB [2] DPC [3] demosaic [4] CCM [5] gamma
                    [6] CSC [7] scaler          (reset 0xC0: RGB out, no scaler)
  0x01C STATUS      RO [0] output locked to the camera
  0x020 CSI         [5:0] data type (reset 0x2B RAW10) [7:6] virtual channel
  0x024 FRAME_SIZE  [15:0] camera width [31:16] height
  0x028-0x034 BLC   R, Gr, Gb, B black levels
  0x038-0x040 WB    R, G, B gains Q4.8 (reset 0x100)
  0x044 DPC_THR     defect threshold (reset 64)
  0x048-0x068 CCM   coefficients c00..c22, signed Q5.10 (reset identity)
  0x06C-0x074 CCM   offsets R, G, B (signed)
  0x078 GAMMA_ADDR  table index for the next GAMMA_DATA write
  0x07C GAMMA_DATA  [7:0] writes table[index], index auto-increments
  0x080 STAT_THR    clip threshold (10-bit, reset 1000)
  0x084-0x08C STAT  RO sums of R, G, B (low 32 bits) of the last frame
  0x090 STAT_PIX    RO pixels, 0x094 STAT_CLIP RO clipped pixels
  0x098 STAT_FRAMES RO
  0x09C-0x0B8 VTG   h active, h front porch, h sync, h back porch,
                    v active, v front porch, v sync, v back porch
  0x0BC SYNC_POL    [0] hsync [1] vsync active high
  0x0C0 LOCK_MAX    genlock: max extra blanking lines (reset 1023)
  0x0C4 START_LEVEL pixels buffered before a frame starts (reset 16)
  0x0C8 AVI         [6:0] VIC [9:8] picture aspect [11:10] RGB range
                    (colour space and colorimetry follow CSC settings)
  0x0CC CSI_FRAMES  RO, 0x0D0 ECC_CORR RO, 0x0D4 ECC_ERR RO,
  0x0D8 CRC_ERR RO, 0x0DC UNDERFLOWS RO, 0x0E0 DPC_CORR RO,
  0x0E4 CSI_OVERFLOW RO (CSI words lost: the bridge FIFO was full)
  0x0E8 OUT_CTRL    [0] LVDS dual link [1] LVDS 18 bpp [2] LVDS JEIDA
                    [4] DSI video [5] DSI EoTp [7:6] DSI virtual channel
                    [8] CSI-2 TX enable [9] CSI-2 TX YUV422 [11:10] its VC
  0x0EC DSI_GAPS    [15:0] LP clocks after a sync packet, [31:16] after pixels
  0x0F0 CSITX_GAP   LP clocks between CSI-2 TX packets
  0x0F4 DSI_CMD     write: queue a DSI command {[24] long, [23:16] data
                    type, [15:0] data / word count} (sent with DSI video off)
  0x0F8 DSI_CMD_BYTE write: [7:0] next payload byte of a long command
  0x0FC TX_STATUS   RO [0] DSI command queue busy
  0x100 DSI_DROPS   RO lines DSI could not send in time
  0x104 CSITX_DROPS RO lines CSI-2 TX could not send in time
  0x108 CSITX_FRAMES RO frames sent by CSI-2 TX
The DSI, CSI-2 TX and LVDS outputs carry the same timed video as HDMI;
panels need RGB (CSC bypassed), CSI-2 YUV422 needs YCbCr (CSC on).
Scaler settings: clear its CTRL.ENABLE, wait for STATUS.BUSY = 0, then
change sizes / steps and enable it again (scaler_ctrl does not support
changing them while a frame is being generated).
  0x10C BUILD_CFG   RO interfaces built: [0] CSI-2 RX [1] HDMI [2] LVDS
                    [3] DSI [4] CSI-2 TX [5] scaler [6] insert point
External interfaces are included or excluded with the `defines in
configuration.sv (compiled first, see scripts/build.f); an excluded
interface has no ports or logic and its registers read as 0.
Clocks - byte_clk (D-PHY), pix_clk (pipeline, registers, video out).
Resets - byte_rst_n, pix_rst_n, synchronous active low; assert both.
```

Describe and handle the edge cases, error recovery, latency and configuration-change rules stated above; where the text is silent, choose the safe option and document it in the file header.

## 6a. Industry reference check

Comparison of section 6 with published engineering references. Every difference is a `TODO(REF-...)` written as a prompt for updating the design.

```text
// Industry reference check - video_pipeline (2026-10-16)
// Sources:
//   [1] MIPI Alliance, "Specification for Camera Serial Interface 2 (CSI-2)" v1.3 (2014):
//   9.1-9.6 low level protocol (DI, WC, 6-bit header ECC, CRC-16 x^16+x^12+x^5+1 seed 0xFFFF),
//   11 data formats (RGB888 0x24 B,G,R; YUV422 8-bit 0x1E U,Y,V,Y; RAW8 0x2A, RAW10 0x2B, RAW12
//   0x2C); vendor summary AMD PG232 https://docs.amd.com/r/5.1-English/pg232-mipi-csi2-rx/MIPI-
//   CSI-2-RX-Controller
//   [2] R. Ramanath, W. E. Snyder, Y. Yoo, M. S. Drew, "Color image processing pipeline", IEEE
//   Signal Processing Magazine 22(1):34-43, 2005, doi:10.1109/MSP.2005.1407713 (black level,
//   white balance, demosaicking, colour transform, tone curve)
//   [3] HDMI Licensing, "High-Definition Multimedia Interface Specification" 1.4b (2011)
//   5.2-5.4 (preambles, guard bands, TERC4, data island, BCH ECC) and CTA-861-G 6.4 (AVI
//   InfoFrame, checksum: all bytes sum to 0); overview https://www.prodigytechno.com/wp-
//   content/uploads/2020/01/TEK-PGY-HDMI_MHL_Application_Notes_V1.0.pdf
//   [4] AMD, "AXI4-Stream Video IP and System Design Guide", UG934 (2022),
//   https://www.amd.com/content/dam/amd/en/documents/products/adaptive-socs-and-
//   fpgas/technologies/axi4-stream-video-ip-and-system-design-guide.pdf - TUSER(0) = SOF on the
//   first pixel, TLAST = EOL
// Published algorithm / equations:
//   Camera ISP chain order (Ramanath 2005): black level -> defect correction -> white balance
//   -> demosaic -> colour correction -> tone curve -> colour space conversion; then scaling and
//   display link.
// Comparison with this IP (section 6):
//   Matches: csi2_rx -> raw unpack -> BLC / WB -> DPC -> demosaic -> CCM -> gamma -> CSC ->
//   scaler -> outputs (HDMI / LVDS / DSI / CSI-2). Note: DPC runs after WB here (industry
//   chains usually correct defects before WB); the result is the same for clamp-based DPC as
//   long as the WB gains are applied to all colours equally in the comparison, so this is
//   documented, not changed.
// TODO(REF-VIDEO_PIPELINE-1) [LOW] DPC placement. Prompt: in
//   ip/video/video_pipeline/src/video_pipeline.sv header, note that DPC follows BLC / WB
//   (Ramanath 2005 places defect correction before white balance) and that the DPC threshold is
//   therefore in white-balanced units; move isp_dpc before isp_blc_wb only if a test shows a
//   difference.
```


## 7. Implementation constraints

- Synthesizable SystemVerilog-2012, technology independent (no vendor primitives; infer RAM and DSP).
- Must work in iverilog 12+ (`-g2012`), Verilator lint (`-Wall`, no UNOPTFLAT or latches) and Yosys (through sv2v: add the `scripts/sv2v` marker file).
- iverilog limits: declare before use; no enum ternaries without casts; no `break`; no arrays of queues; no `wait` on function calls; no declarations inside nested loop bodies of static initial blocks.
- No combinational path from a ready input back to a ready output; hoist scratch variables (no latches); split control and data `always_ff` blocks.
- One statement per line (`a <= b; c <= d;` is two lines; `if (x) y <= 1; else y <= 0;` is four).
- Instantiations: one parameter per line in `#( ... )` and one port per line, closing with `) u_name (` and `);` at the instance's indentation; a port-group macro is one port on its own line.
- Check with `python3 ip/scripts/sv_format.py --check <files>` (it can also rewrite: whitespace only, token-checked).
- Resources: Last Yosys synth_xilinx (7-series) result: about 7675 LUTs, 6096 flip-flops, 42 DSP48E1, 6 RAMB36E1, 21 RAMB18E1. Stay within about this budget.

Read the file header template from `ip/docs/HEADER_TEMPLATE.txt` and start every file you create (RTL, testbench, test tasks, scripts, file lists, Makefile) with that header, filled in: Filename, Author: FPGA Cores 4 U, Description, Date. In RTL the Description is the specification (behaviour, register map, parameters, clocks, resets, clock-domain crossings, latency, resources, errors); in testbenches it says what is checked; test-task files list every task with a one-line description (the test list scripts use it).

Header template file: `ip/docs/HEADER_TEMPLATE.txt`   (replace with your own template file if needed)

## 9. Guidelines

Follow the design guidelines in `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md` (complete rules; this prompt wins where it sets a value explicitly). In short:

- Synthesizable, technology-independent SystemVerilog-2012; behavioural models behind `` `ifdef SYNTHESIS `` black boxes; iverilog / Verilator / Yosys clean.
- Layout: one statement per line; one parameter and one port per line in instantiations; two-space indent; a comment on every port.
- Naming: `lower_snake_case` modules and files, `u_` instances, `g_` generate blocks, `UPPER_CASE` parameters, `_i` / `_o` / `_n` / `_t` port suffixes, `s_axis_` / `m_axis_` / `s_axil_` buses.
- Clocks and resets per domain, every crossing through a CDC technique (see the clocks section).
- AXI4-Stream data with back-pressure, AXI4-Lite control (ID / INFO registers, SLVERR out of range), defined switch-over points for configuration changes.
- Self-checking testbench with an independent model, named `test_<what>` tasks in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, gaps and back-pressure, a mutation check, 100 % code coverage.
- Diagrams: module and instance names, arrows from output to input, no crossing lines, every clock and reset domain labelled.

Guidelines file: `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md`   (replace with your own guidelines file if needed)

| Code coverage | Verilator `--coverage` + `verilator_coverage`, `ip/tools/cov/cov_report.py` | `make cov` / `ip/scripts/run_cov.sh` (LCOV `coverage.info`; vendor simulators: native coverage) |
| Formatting | `ip/scripts/sv_format.py` | `--check` before delivery |
| Synthesis | Yosys (Xilinx 7-series flow, sv2v where needed) | `make synth`; alternative Synplify (`SYNTHESIS`) |
| Place and route (optional) | Vivado | `PLACE_ROUTE` in `ip/.tools`, once a device is chosen |
| Diagrams | Graphviz (`dot`) | `make diagram` / `make diagrams` |
| Firmware (py_soc) | Python 3 + `ip/cpu/py_core/tools/pyc.py` | run by `scripts/run_sim.sh` |
| Test list | `ip/scripts/list_tests.py` | `run_sim.sh --list-tests` / `make list-tests` |
| Prompts and docs | `make_ip_prompts.py`, `gen_docs.py`, `make_block_diagrams.py` | regenerate after a change |

## 12. Verification requirements

The reference testbench checks the following; the new testbench must cover at least the same:

```text
System testbench for video_pipeline: MIPI CSI-2 camera in,
HDMI / DVI out. A camera model mosaics a synthetic RGB scene into an
RGGB RAW10 image (with black level and two defective pixels) and streams
it continuously as CSI-2 frames on 2 D-PHY lanes (csi2_bfm).
The TMDS output is decoded by hdmi_bfm. A bit-exact model of the
chain (black level, white balance, defect correction, demosaic, CCM,
gamma table, CSC, scaler) predicts every output pixel. Scenarios:
  1. full ISP, HDMI, RGB out (CSC bypassed), gamma 2.2 table
  2. full ISP, HDMI, YCbCr 4:4:4 BT.709 (AVI InfoFrame must follow)
  3. everything bypassed, DVI: grey raw >> 2
  4. a mixed bypass mask
  5. scaler 1:1 and 2:1 (display 16x12), routed through scaler_bilinear
  6. test pattern
  7. a camera header bit error: corrected, image unchanged
  8. the other outputs, same frame: LVDS (decoded OpenLDI VESA words),
     MIPI CSI-2 TX (looped into a second csi2_rx) and MIPI DSI
     (dsi_bfm; an init command first, then VSS / HSS and pixel
     packets), all compared with the model
The interfaces follow configuration.sv: excluded ones are not connected
and not checked. Scenarios 1-7 need the camera input and HDMI; without
the camera, scenario 8 checks every output against the test pattern.
BUILD_CFG must report the configuration. +quick runs scenario 8 only.
plus the status registers (CSI frames, ECC / CRC counters, defects
corrected, statistics against the model, lock). Prints TEST PASSED on
success.
The test tasks are in tests/video_pipeline_tests.sv (`included).
```

Also: an independent reference model (not a copy of the RTL); random input gaps and output back-pressure on every stream; register readback; edge cases; a mutation check (break one rule, show the testbench fails).

Every simulation script names the tests it can run: `ip/scripts/run_sim.sh video_pipeline --list-tests` prints them (and every run prints them at its start). Put each test in its own `test_<what>` task in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, listed with a one-line description in that file's header.

Tests of the reference design (the new design must provide at least these):

| Testbench | Test | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `video_pipeline_tb` | `video_pipeline_tb` | one test: System testbench for video_pipeline: MIPI CSI-2 camera in, HDMI / DVI out. |

Code coverage (`make cov`, `ip/scripts/run_cov.sh`): every target is 100 % by default. A target may be lowered only here, per metric, with the reason; every item left uncovered is listed with its justification (unreachable by design, tied-off parameter, ...).

| Metric | Target |
|--------|--------|
| Line (statement) | 100 % |
| Branch (if / case arms, ternaries) | 100 % |
| Expression / condition | 100 % |
| Toggle (every bit 0->1 and 1->0) | 100 % |
| FSM state and transition | 100 % |
| Functional (a cover point / cover property per requirement, mode and corner) | 100 % |
| Assertions (every SVA property exercised, none failing) | 100 % |

Pass criteria: `make -C video/video_pipeline test` passes, every coverage target met, Verilator lint clean, `sv_format.py --check` clean, `make synth` passes.
